summary: Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole debut put a September rate hike firmly on the table, citing PCE inflation at 3.7% with over half the basket still rising faster than 3%, pushing rate-hike odds to roughly 57% from 35% before the speech. The two-year Treasury yield hit its highest since July near 4.32%, the dollar firmed, and gold slid roughly 3% — pressuring safe-haven sentiment even as crypto and bonds held relative ground on the week.
tweet: Warsh's Jackson Hole hawkishness flipped a majority of investors to expect a September hike, sending yields and the dollar higher while gold sold off sharply.
